It recounts the past deeds (*apadāna*) of the elder (*thera*) Cunda. While no specific English title is registered for the text on SuttaCentral, five modern translations across five languages are recorded in its catalog [SuttaCentral].

In addition, repetitive formulaic and biographical verses connect it with numerous other poems in the *Therāpadāna*, such as the *Udenattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 412), *Ānandattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 12), and *Mogharājattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 37) [DharmaNexus].
